How BIM professionals are assessed.

The evaluation criteria ENGISOFT uses before a BIM professional is shortlisted: experience, software, technical judgement, a practical task and communication.

Stages

Six layers of evidence.

01

Experience verification

Employment history and project exposure reviewed against what the candidate claims.

02

Software assessment

Proficiency tested in the tools the role needs: Revit, Navisworks, ACC, Civil 3D and others.

03

Technical interview

Discipline-specific questions with an engineer, covering standards, LOD and coordination judgement.

04

Practical BIM test

A time-boxed exercise reproducing a realistic modelling or coordination task.

05

Portfolio verification

Work samples reviewed where the candidate and former employers authorise it.

06

Communication & standards

English communication and knowledge of BIM execution and information standards.

Evaluation criteria

What each stage looks for.

01

Modelling accuracy

Geometry, levels, LOD and parameters correct against the brief.

02

Standards compliance

Naming, templates, worksets and view standards applied without prompting.

03

Coordination judgement

Recognising which clashes matter and proposing workable resolutions.

04

Documentation

Clean sheets, annotation and schedules generated from the model.

05

Speed and organisation

Completing the practical task in the time allowed, with a tidy model.

06

Communication

Explaining decisions clearly in English to a project team.

Sample reports

What you receive.

Each shortlisted profile shows the stages completed, the result of each and the date it was verified. Anonymised sample assessment reports can be shared on request.
